vol1_location: l.7756-7800, Ch.9 end (p.419) / Ch.10 start (p.420-421): jartila vidhi unauthoritative, ajakṣīra clause, apaśavo vā anye, other-Śākhā reading, person-difference
explanation: Same: jartila-vidhi granted unauthoritative, real act is 'ajakṣīreṇa juhoti', censure is praise, valid for another Śākhā's student, like another's food in another stage; Taittirīya 'vāyava sthopāyava stha' opens the Śākhā-difference example.
Both: Vājasaneyins omit upāyavastha, Śatapatha restates and rejects it; Sūktavāka 'sūpāvasānā'/'sūpacaraṇā' resolved by difference of performers (Vol 1 'difference in the sacrificers').
Same references: Pūrva-mīmāṃsā 10.8 option of taking Ṣoḍaśin, 2.1 apūrva for future fruit, Brahma-sūtra 1.4.14 reconciles Śruti on the cause; sūtra 'asadvyapadeśān neti cen na…' begins (continued).

vol1_location: l.7878-7960 (p.423-425), Ch.10: 'blind man and the post' proverb
explanation: New: 'the argument of the post and the robber' (Sanskrit supplied: स्थाण्वन्धन्यायः, 'the sthāṇu-andha maxim'); Vol 1: 'the proverb about the blind man and the post' with Nirukta 'naiṣa sthāṇor aparādho yad enam andho na śaknoti'. The new English misread अन्ध as a robber; Vol 1 (and the Sanskrit as supplied) supports 'blind man'. The rest of the unit (asat = unmanifest; Jaimini 1.1.2 and 1.1.5 on authority of injunction; Vyāsa śāstrayonitva; tattu samanvayāt) agrees; sūtra number given 1.1.3 for 'tat tu samanvayāt' in the supplied text, Vol 1 has 1-1-4.

Same: Jaimini establishes authority of arthavāda with great effort; first the pūrvapakṣa sūtra 'āmnāyasya kriyārthatvāt…'; since revelation has sacrifice as its aim, what does not serve it is pointless, called 'anitya'.
Same examples (so'rodīt, vapām udakhidat, devā vai devayajanam…); anitya = not in itself non-eternal (Veda beginningless) but lacking the eternal duty (nityakārya) like poetry and ordinary talk.
Same: authority in own meaning anticipated; three kinds of conflict (scripture, sight, both); 'stenaṃ mano 'nṛtavādinī vāk' conflicts with scripture.
Same three examples: dhūma eva agner divā dadṛśe (sight), na caitad vidmo… brāhmaṇā vā (sight/perception), ko hi tad veda (scripture and sight, via svargakāmo yajeta).
Same: fruit-statements do not hold; examples Garga-trirātra 'śobhate 'sya mukham' and Veda-study 'asya prajāyāṃ vājī jāyate'; no such fruit seen in students.

Same: other-world fruit statements (pūrṇāhutyā sarvān kāmān, paśubandhayājī sarvāñ lokān, aśvamedha crossing brahmin-killing) would make later rites pointless; mere knowledge of the aśvamedha would suffice.
Same: 'na pṛthivyām agniś cetavyo nāntarikṣe na divi' has no occasion in sky and atmosphere; 'babaraḥ prāvāhaṇir akāmayata' brings a non-eternal.
Same: connection with non-eternal implies human origin, arthavāda fully without authority is the pūrvapakṣa; siddhānta sūtra 'vidhinā tv ekavākyatvāt stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ'.
Same: 'tu' rejects the objection; 'vāyur vai kṣepiṣṭhā' with 'vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabheta'; vidhi expects men's action, praise engages men.

Same: tradition (study with restrictions) is equal for vidhi and arthavāda, so not inattention; sūtra 'āprāptā cānupapattiḥ…' answers the conflict objection because the meaning of the words is not part of the performance.
Same: no contradiction with the scripture since theft is not enjoined as practice, only the word's meaning is stated (the new text's NOTE on prāptā/aprāptā does not touch the sense).

Same: vetasa-śākhā/avakā vidhi vs 'āpo vai śāntāḥ' (difference of subject), answered by guṇavāda; Kashmir/Devadatta analogy; cane and avakā born of calm waters, hence calm and allay what is unfavourable.

New: 'silver is not to be given on the sacred grass' (barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam); Vol 1 English: 'silver is not to be used for the fee of the priest' (though its Sanskrit quotes the same 'tasmād barhiṣi na deyam'). Same argument about no weeping in the house; both say the silver-from-tears story is unreal.
Same argument (hornless goat praised through Prajāpati's act, offspring and cattle); Vol 1 English says 'entrails' where the new English (and the Sanskrit vapām) says 'omentum'.

vol1_location: l.8560-8592 (p.446, 448; p.447 not present in Vol 1)
explanation: Same: Āditya prāyaṇīya caru praised by the confusion of directions, Aditi removing it; praise may use non-existent matter ('your hair/tuft grows, drink with faith'); only the part of p.447 is missing in Vol 1, so the Aditi sentences could be checked only from p.446/448.
Same: answer to 'stenaṃ mano' by 'rūpāt prāyāt' (gold in hand, mind concealed like a thief, speech mostly untrue, Devadatta analogy); answer to 'dhūma eva' by 'dūrabhūyastvāt'.
Same: arthavāda praises the two mantras 'agnir jyotir…' evening and 'sūryo jyotir…' morning; flame not seen by day, only flame by night; great distance, trees on hill look like grass.

Same argument ('na caitad vidmaḥ' is difficulty of knowing, paramour's son seen, no clash with sight). New: 'even a non-brahmin would become a brahmin' (subject unnamed); Vol 1 English: 'the priest becomes a brahmin'; the Sanskrit in Vol 1 (l.8658) agrees with the new.
Same: door-of-eastern-hall vidhi, smoke avoided (visible), heaven future (ākālika), desire to obtain (īpsā), ignorance statement like not knowing grandchildren's future.
Same: Garga-trirātra vidhi, mere knowledge brings face-glory, how much more the performance; face beautified as by an ornament, 'shines' metaphorical.
Same: 'vājī jāyate' arthavāda of the Veda-reciting vidhi, a fortiori; the son learns from the father and obtains food by gifts.

Same: 'all' is relative (all brahmins of one's house), only fruit of the rite at hand; absent pūrṇāhuti the ādhāna is maimed, Āhavanīya fires fit for Agnihotra, etc.; other oblations may also do this without harm.

Same: dravya-saṃskāra-karmasu parārthatvāt phalaśrutir arthavādaḥ; paśubandha fruit is final, so sūtra 'phalasya karmaniṣpatteḥ…lokavat': increase in quantity or quality (khārī of rice for one niṣka/another niṣka; cloth vs silk); mental killing crossed by knowledge, actual by aśvamedha.

Same: last two (atmosphere/sky prohibition; Babara) answered as before; 'hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya cetavyam'; restatement of what is always established praises the vidhi like Vāyu's swiftness; Babara = Vāyu with the sound 'babara', given to blowing/going.
Same: summary verses of the Saṅgraha (vāyur vā… arthavāda authoritative; vidhi and arthavāda need each other, hence one sentence, authority in dharma); authority of whole Veda established.
Same: Veda of human origin as pūrvapakṣa; 'vedāṃś caike sannikarṣaṃ puruṣākhyā'; the Kāṭhaka etc. names show authors.
Same: names might only mean propagators; 'anityadarśanāc ca': Babara Prāvāhaṇi, Kusuruvinda Auddālaki; inference 'sentence like Kālidāsa's'.
Same: 'tu' rejects non-eternity; priority of word already stated (autpattika sūtra); 'ākhyā pravacanāt' answers the names; 'paraṃ tu śrutisāmānyamātram': Babara is Vāyu with sound ba-ba-ra.

Same: trees and serpents sat (sattra), like the speech of a madman ('jaradgavo gāyati madrakāṇi'); answer: if made, no application of the rite; bhāvanā with three parts (feed brahmins example); arthavāda purport is praise, 'how much more' the sentient; and absence of an author.
Same Saṅgraha verses: human origin (Kāṭhaka naming, sentencehood) refuted; names from teaching; no author found, so non-human.

Same: śāstrayonitvāt does not prove human origin; 'ata eva ca nityatvam', 'vācā virūpa nityayā', 'anādinidhanā nityā vāg utsṛṣṭā svayambhuvā'. New gives 'eternal like space in practical use'; Vol 1 English adds 'for all who have not obtained final release'. Sūtra numbers 1.1.3 / 1.2.29 (new, 'वे. १।१|3', '१।२।२९') versus Vol 1 1-1-3 / 1-3-29.
Same objection that Veda = mantra+brāhmaṇa lacks a definition, answered by the 7th and 8th adhikaraṇas of the first pāda of Mīmāṃsā chapter 2.

Same: seventh adhikaraṇa verses (there is no definition because of non-pervasion; the sacrificers' usage is the faultless definition); 'ahe budhniya mantraṃ me gopāya' recited at the Ādhāna (Vol 1 cites Tai.Brā. 1-2-1-26, new reads 86).

New: 'a mantra ends in a verb' (read evaṃ tiṅpadānto from the damaged evam-atti-padānto); Vol 1 Sanskrit (l.9381) reads 'asipadānto mantra uttamapuruṣānto mantraḥ' and its English 'ends in the second person… excludes all that end in the first person': the supported reading is 'ends in -asi (second person)', which fits the pairing with 'first person' and not 'verb'. Rest of unit agrees: kapiñjala vidhi-form, manana = over-pervasion into brāhmaṇa, uru prathasva, agnim īḷe, iṣe tvā (ends in tvā), agna ā yāhi vītaye.

Same: agnīd agnīn vihara (command/directory), adhaḥ svid (inquiry/'philosophical'), ambe ambike (lamentation), pṛcchāmi (question), answer; verse 'ṛṣayo 'pi padārthānāṃ…'; usage is the definition; eighth adhikaraṇa 'no definition of brāhmaṇa because the Veda's extent is not settled'. Vol 1 transliterations of the question/answer lines are garbled ('pruchcha api tva…', 'venim achchhah'); second half of the verse is damaged in the new (NOTE) and given in full in Vol 1.
